title: Sound Waves
page_title: Sound Waves | Cambridge (CIE) IGCSE Combined Science Revision Notes 2023

blocks.md:
- Sound waves are produced by **vibrating** sources
- A **medium** is needed to transmit sound waves

  - This means if there are no molecules, such as in a **vacuum**, then the sound can’t travel through it

- When a sound wave comes into contact with a solid, the wave vibrations are** transferred** to the solid

  - For example, sound waves can cause a drinking glass to vibrate
  - If the glass vibrates too much the movement causes the glass to shatter

- Sound waves are [Longitudinal ](https://www.savemyexams.com/igcse/science/cie/combined-science/23/physics/revision-notes/waves/general-properties-of-waves/transverse-longitudinal-waves/)waves
- Longitudinal waves travel in air as a series of **compressions** and** rarefactions**:

  - **Compressions** are regions of higher pressure due to particles being closer together
  - **Rarefactions** are regions of of lower pressure due to particles being spaced further apart

blocks.alt: Compressions and rarefactions, IGCSE & GCSE Physics revision notes

blocks.md: ***Sound is a longitudinal wave consisting of compressions and rarefactions - these are areas where the pressure of the air in the pipe varies with the wave***

blocks.label: Exam Hint
blocks.md: When describing compressions and rarefactions, make sure to use the correct terms. It is best to refer to them as regions of high and low pressures of particles instead of the particles being more 'bunched up' or 'far apart', as this is too vague and not very scientific!
